articles.headline: Brandon Miller scores career-high 39 points as Hornets beat Wizards 110-103
articles.description: — Brandon Miller scored a career-high 39 points and the Charlotte Hornets beat the Washington Wizards 110-103 on Monday night for their third win in four games to open the season.
articles.headlineJa: ブランドン・ミラーがキャリアハイの39得点を記録、ホーネッツがウィザーズを110-103で撃破
articles.descriptionJa: ブランドン・ミラーがキャリアハイとなる39得点を挙げ、月曜の夜、シャーロット・ホーネッツはワシントン・ウィザーズを110-103で下し、開幕4試合で3勝目を挙げた。
articles.body:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- — Brandon Miller scored a career-high 39 points and the Charlotte Hornets beat the Washington Wizards 110-103 on Monday night for their third win in four games to open the season.


              Starters Coby White (left calf) and Kon Knueppel (left hamstring) and top reserve Grant Williams (right hamstring) each have yet to play this season for the Hornets, who have managed their absences well so far.


              Miller scored 27 points in the middle two quarters as Charlotte took control.


              The fourth-year guard topped 30 points for the 14th time in his career and scored 30 in back-to-back games for the fourth time. A 2023 first-round pick out of Alabama, Miller a week ago signed a five-year, $209 million contract extension.


              Naz Reid finished with 18 points and 12 rebounds for the Hornets, who had a seemingly comfortable 98-84 lead with 5:15 to play.


              But the Wizards (2-2), who were seeking their first 3-1 start since the 2022-23 season, knocked down five 3-pointers down the stretch and got as close as 103-100 with 1:13 to play.


              Miller hit a jumper and later made a free throw for his final three points to make it 106-100 with 38.3 seconds left.


              Grayson Allen added 15 points and Moussa Diabate had 11 points and 17 rebounds for Charlotte.


              Anthony Davis had 29 points and 10 rebounds, Trae Young scored 22 points and Kyshawn George added 20 points for Washington. Wizards forward Justin Champagnie suffered a right foot injury in the first quarter and did not return.


              Washington was again without A.J. Dybantsa, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NBA draft, whose debut has been delayed by a sprained left ankle. 


              Davis' personal win streak against Charlotte ended. The Hornets had lost 10 straight games in which the oft-injured Davis had played against them, dating to March 2016.


              Up next
              Wizards: Visit Cleveland on Wednesday.


              Hornets: Visit Detroit on Wednesday.


              ------

articles.headline: Jay-Z's greatest sports lyrics, ranked ahead of his Super Bowl show
articles.description: The Super Bowl headliner's catalog is packed with sports references -- here are the ones that top our list.
articles.headlineJa: スーパーボウルのパフォーマンスを前に、ジェイ・Zの最高のスポーツ関連リリックをランク付け
articles.descriptionJa: スーパーボウルのヘッドライナーを務める彼の楽曲にはスポーツへの言及が満載だ。その中でも、私たちのリストのトップに選んだものを紹介する。
articles.body:
One of the greatest rappers of all time -- or the greatest in many eyes -- Jay-Z is still out here adding to his legacy. We finally have an answer to a question that has hovered over 2026 ever since Jay-Z dubbed this year all about offense in his March 2026 cover story with GQ.

Would Jigga actually select himself to perform on the Super Bowl stage he helped revitalize?

The answer is: you damn right, he will. So while we don't yet know the teams who'll be taking the field, we do know the man born Shawn Carter will be there at the 50-yard line waiting on them.

History and Hov are well acquainted.

The show is going to be full of trademark Jay hits. It'll also be full of sports lyrics, because if there's one thing Hov knows, it's sports. From deep dives into Michael Jordan history to NASCAR, scrambling quarterbacks and everything in between, a Jay-Z album might have more sports references than "SportsCenter" does.

With such a robust history of sports references, we decided to rank his 10 best, most unexpected and clever. As they say, "the list is fluid."

10. "And I sport fly s--- I should win an ESPY" - "Party Life" (2007)

 This is a little bit of bias, so pardon us. Jay-Z shouting out the ESPYS is just pretty cool. Now he just needs to pull up and host or perform one of these years. When he does, he has our full permission to rap this exact lyric. Heck, he could even win an ESPY for the reference alone. -- David Dennis Jr.

9. "It's Hov tradition, Jeff Gordon of rap/ I'm back to claim pole position, holla at ya boy" -- "Never Let Me Down" (2004)

 If there's one NASCAR driver who's going to get referenced in rap songs, it's going to be Jeff Gordon. His rap credentials are certified. It doesn't get more certified than a nod from Hov. As always, there's a double meaning here. In 2004, Jay had taken his short-lived retirement, and this was his claim that he's back to lead the way like he never left. Well, he kind of never did. -- David Dennis Jr.

8. "You cats is home screaming the fight's on/ I'm in the 1500 seats, watching Tyson/ Same night, same fight/ But one of us cats ain't playing right/ I let you tell it" -- "I Love The Dough" (1997)

One of rap history's great what-ifs is how much more music Jay-Z and his close friend the Notorious B.I.G. could've made if the latter hadn't been slain in 1997. The Mike Tyson reference here calls to mind Jay and Roc-A-Fella Records' 1995 trip to Sin City to watch Tyson's first post-prison fight against Peter McNeely. This same fight would also live in another Jay-Z classic, "Can I Live." -- Justin Tinsley

7. "I don't even know y'all name/ I'm too big for ya, the rap LeBron James" -- "Blow The Whistle" (2008)

Let this next sentence marinate. LeBron James has been playing in the NBA so long that Jay-Z once defended him against ... DeShawn Stevenson and Soulja Boy. articles.headline: Jay-Z's road to the Super Bowl: Were the clues there all along?
articles.description: With Hov headed to SoFi Stadium's halftime stage in Los Angeles, we revisit the breadcrumbs that might have pointed us there.
articles.headlineJa: ジェイ・Zのスーパーボウルへの道：そのヒントは最初からあったのか？
articles.descriptionJa: ジェイ・ZがロサンゼルスのSoFiスタジアムのハーフタイムステージに登場するにあたり、そこへ導く手がかりとなっていたかもしれない要素を振り返る。
articles.body:
"I said no to the Super Bowl: You need me, I don't need you. Every night we in the end zone, tell the NFL we in stadiums too." -- Jay-Z, "Apes---"

The man who famously rapped about turning down the Super Bowl in 2018 has changed his tune.

Jay-Z is headed to SoFi Stadium to headline the Super Bowl LXI halftime show, putting one of hip-hop's deepest catalogs on football's biggest stage. Apparently, "I don't need you" left a little room for "see you in Inglewood."

Hov is already well acquainted with the operation. Roc Nation, the entertainment company he founded in 2008, has partnered with the NFL since August 2019 as the league's "live music entertainment strategist." He has helped shape the halftime spectacle from behind the scenes, beginning with Shakira and Jennifer Lopez's performance at Super Bowl LIV in 2020.

Now, after a run of headliners including Kendrick Lamar and Bad Bunny, the businessman (read as: business, man) helping put the show together is putting himself on the bill. From the boardroom to the halftime stage, consider it a promotion.

Jay taking his talents to midfield might surprise anyone still holding him to those "Apes---" bars. But saying no isn't the same as saying never, and a closer look suggests this moment didn't come entirely out of nowhere.

Has Hov been telling us all along? Here are the hints that hit a little differently now.

A little stadium practice: On to the next stage

Jay-Z got a few stadium reps alongside his wife, Beyoncé, with his three surprise appearances on her Cowboy Carter Tour in 2025, popping up in Paris, Atlanta and Las Vegas.

His June 22 appearance at the Atlanta Falcons' Mercedes-Benz Stadium marked the couple's first live performance together in seven years, with the 2003 hit "Crazy in Love" among the songs on the set list. He also made a surprise appearance for the July 26 tour finale at the Las Vegas Raiders' Allegiant Stadium.

A few guest verses don't necessarily signal a halftime audition, but in hindsight, those stadium cameos could be read as an intriguing warmup.

'Politics as usual' in Philly

Before plotting a showing on football's biggest stage, Hov got back to headlining in Philadelphia. Announced March 17, his Roots Picnic appearance came with a warmup: an invite-only preshow the night before at The Foundry.

His May 30 Roots Picnic set marked his first solo headlining show since at least 2019, and the city was familiar territory. Jay-Z launched the Made in America there in 2012, turning Labor Day weekend on the Benjamin Franklin Parkway into a recurring destination for music's biggest names. In hindsight, that experience bringing stars together feels like a fitting prelude to Roc Nation's halftime work.

His return to the City of Brotherly Love came with a reunion, bringing out longtime Philly-based collaborators including Beanie Sigel, Freeway, Peedi Crakk, Memphis Bleek and the Young Gunz. He sported a new look, too: an afro (in place of his freeform locs) that honored his f

articles.headline: Kane's long road to Ballon d'Or glory ends with his crowning moment
articles.description: After a remarkable year for Bayern Munich and England, Harry Kane becoming the world's best player is the ultimate reward for years of perseverance.
articles.headlineJa: ケイン、バロンドール獲得への長い道のりが最高の瞬間で結実
articles.descriptionJa: バイエルン・ミュンヘンとイングランドにとって驚異的な1年を経て、ハリー・ケインが世界最高の選手となったことは、長年の忍耐に対する究極の報酬である。
articles.body:
LONDON -- It is nine years since Harry Kane lingered at the back of the London Palladium at the end of a soccer awards show.

The Best FIFA Football Awards in 2017 had just concluded with Cristiano Ronaldo handed the men's top prize in addition to leading a team of the year including Lionel Messi, Neymar, Sergio Ramos and Gianluigi Buffon.

As the audience filed out and a few mere mortals loitered in the hope of a selfie, Kane stood near the exit, casting a longing stare at the winners on stage. He has dreamed all his life of being in their place, considered in the same breath as the game's greats.

On Monday, at the same storied West End venue, about nine miles from his birthplace in Leytonstone, he finally is. Sat next to Lamine Yamal with last year's winner Rodri one place further away, Kane kept company with the elite. And then he joined them.

Last week in Munich, he told reporters he had found the wait to learn the winner "very stressful" for himself and his family. The final few hours on Monday won't have helped. The rain present earlier in the day subsided, but the controversy did not.

Less than three hours before the ceremony was due to start, the official website published a profile of Kane as the 2026 Ballon d'Or winner. Alongside one for Kylian Mbappé and one for Yamal. They were swiftly deleted. The entire ceremony was then delayed by 45 minutes with no official reason given, amid some speculation that the notorious London traffic was responsible.

Kane won on the undercard -- the Gerd Müller Men's Award or the Striker of the Year -- to cheers from the locals in the audience. The raucous reaction from the cheap seats before addressing the crowd was a prelude to what followed. It was palpably welcome but not, by itself, an indication of the big one: Striker of the Year is not decided by vote but simply by goals, and Kane's 73 was the best in the men's game.

Having waited for over a decade to live this moment, a few extra minutes made no difference in the end.

"Wow, wow, wow," he said after taking the stage before thanking Tottenham Hotspur by saying "I wouldn't be where I am without you" in a moment of typical class.

Monday's Ballon d'Or triumph is the crowning moment for a player whose story of relentless professionalism and determined aspiration serves as an exemplar for any young player. British media is often criticized for prematurely building up players to an impossible level, only to then knock them down when that level is inevitably never reached.

Kane has always been a different case. He publicly judged himself against Ronaldo and Messi, two of the best in history, and used their devastating consistency as a target to match.

His numbers since joining Bayern Munich are staggering: 158 goals in 156 matches following a €120 million move from Tottenham in 2023. The Ballon d'Or voting period takes into account August 2025 to the end of the World Cup in July.

articles.headline: Suddenly thin Thunder lose Alex Caruso to ankle sprain
articles.description: The already-thin Oklahoma City Thunder lost guard Alex Caruso to a right ankle sprain in Monday night's game vs. the Suns.
articles.headlineJa: サンダー、アレックス・カルーソーが足首の捻挫で離脱、戦力不足に拍車
articles.descriptionJa: すでに層の薄いオクラホマシティ・サンダーは、月曜夜のサンズ戦でガードのアレックス・カルーソーが右足首を捻挫し、戦線を離脱した。
articles.body:
OKLAHOMA CITY -- Oklahoma City Thunder guard Alex Caruso was assisted to the locker room during the first half of Monday night's game against the Phoenix Suns and later ruled out with a right ankle sprain.

The injury is ill-timed for the Thunder, as Caruso was expected to see increased minutes in the wake of long-term injuries to starters Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace.

 

Caruso came up limping in the final two minutes of the second quarter with the Thunder leading 61-47.

Williams and Wallace were hurt in Sunday night's 108-101 win over the Clippers and will require surgery. A third starter, Chet Holmgren, missed Monday's game with patellar tendinitis in the right knee.

Ajay Mitchell started for Williams and gave the Thunder a lift with 18 points in the first half. Jared McCain started for Wallace and contributed 10 points. Caruso added nine points for Oklahoma City, which led 67-53 at halftime.

The Thunder were also without star big man Chet Holmgren, who sat with knee inflammation.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Manchester City charges: Features, explainers, what's next after guilty verdict
articles.description: ESPN has you covered with everything you need to know about the latest in the Manchester City scandal.
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・シティの容疑：特集、解説、有罪判決後の今後の展開
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・シティのスキャンダルに関する最新情報について、ESPNが知っておくべきすべてをまとめてお伝えします。
articles.body:
After an investigation spanning years, Manchester City were found guilty on more than 100 charges of serious breaches of Premier League financial regulations. The decision is a major development in one of the biggest scandals in soccer history, but the saga is far from over.

What happens next? What does the ruling mean for England's dominant force over the past decade, its fans and its players? ESPN's writers have you covered on every angle, from transfer implications to the mood at City's rival clubs.

Check back here for the latest as this story continues to unfold.

O'Hanlon: Man City cheated because the Premier League's rules gave them no other choice

The Premier League is unfair: Some teams are allowed to spend more than everyone else. So, of course Man City cheated to win.

Tighe: Man City's alternate universe: Guardiola, Haaland to Arsenal? Arteta to PSG?

What would the sport have looked like if City had not spent in the way that they did? Who would have won the eight league titles? Where would the superstars (like Erling Haaland) they signed have gone instead? And what would manager Pep Guardiola's career have looked like without a decade-long stint in Manchester?

Lindop: Was epic Man City-Liverpool rivalry all a sham after cheating scandal?

Under Jürgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola, Liverpool and Man City pushed the Premier League's standards higher than ever. But was it all a sham?

Dawson: 'We're Not Really Here': As Man City sanctions loom, it's the fans who suffer

Manchester City's financial malfeasance could send the club back down the football pyramid, a place where fans of a certain age are very familiar.

Olley: Arsenal fight back to win as Premier League resumes under cloud of Man City verdict

Does Arsenal's comeback win over Leeds close the gap on leaders Man City, or extend their own lead at the top? This is the perpetual uncertainty that hangs over the Premier League now.

Ogden: What's next for Man City? Appeals, possible punishments, how long it could take

Man City have appealed the Premier League's guilty verdict, while the sanctions board also begins its work on figuring out appropriate punishments. So what happens next, and what is the possible timeline?

Marcotti: We don't get Man City guilty verdict without hacker Rui Pinto, but it doesn't make him a hero

It's worth reminding ourselves that the Manchester City case, which has rocked English football to its foundation, would never have seen the light of day without a spiky-haired college dropout turned self-taught hacker named Rui Pinto.

O'Hanlon: Mock draft: How would Premier League teams pick if Man City cheating scandal took a turn?

Now that Manchester City have been found to have cheated on a huge scale, anything is on the table -- maybe even an American-style Premier League draft?

articles.headline: Pacers' Ben Sheppard to undergo surgery for torn meniscus
articles.description: Indiana guard Ben Sheppard will undergo surgery for a torn meniscus on Wednesday.
articles.headlineJa: ペイサーズのベン・シェパード、半月板損傷のため手術へ
articles.descriptionJa: インディアナのガード、ベン・シェパードは水曜日に半月板損傷の手術を受ける予定だ。
articles.body:
MILWAUKEE -- Indiana Pacers guard Ben Sheppard will undergo surgery for a torn meniscus on Wednesday.

Pacers coach Rick Carlisle gave the update on Sheppard before Indiana's game with the Milwaukee Bucks on Monday night. Sheppard appeared in the Pacers' season-opening 123-120 victory at New Orleans but hasn't played since.

The 6-foot-6 guard averaged 7.1 points per game in 65 games last season.

Ivica Zubac managed to walk into Fiserv Forum without a walking boot, one night after the 7-footer sprained his left ankle during a 136-109 triumph at Brooklyn, Carlisle said. Carlisle said Zubac had a slight limp and didn't offer a timetable for the center's return.

The Pacers also played Monday night without Andrew Nembhard because of a back issue.

articles.headline: Man United tight-lipped after Carrick's Monday visit to Carrington
articles.description: Michael Carrick has left Carrington after Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox held talks over his future.
articles.headlineJa: マン・U、キャリックの月曜日のキャリントン訪問後、沈黙を守る
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッドのオマール・ベラーダCEOとジェイソン・ウィルコックス・フットボール・ディレクターがマイケル・キャリックの将来について協議した後、彼はキャリントンを後にした。
articles.body:
Michael Carrick has left Carrington after Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox held talks over his future, with the club still not tipping its hand about the under-fire coach's position.

The popular former Red Devils midfielder not only steadied the ship after Ruben Amorim's rocky reign but helped it change course as his January arrival inspired the side's rise to third in the Premier League.

Carrick's impressive stint saw him rewarded with a two-year deal to stay on as United boss, but just five months later he is facing the sack following Sunday's 3-0 Old Trafford loss to Bournemouth.

Talks over the managerial situation followed that defeat and continued after Berrada and Wilcox arrived at the Carrington training complex on Monday morning, the Press Association understands.

Carrick arrived at the training ground shortly before 2 p.m. as United Under-21s took on Hull -- the side that helped ensure United got their Premier League season off to a nightmare start -- in a behind closed doors friendly.

The head coach left the training complex just before 5pm, shortly after Wilcox departed, having spent around three hours at Carrington.

But the wait for clarity on Carrick's future rumbles on ahead of the United players' return for training on Tuesday following a day off. Carrick is expected to oversee practice at Carrington on Tuesday.

Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann are potential replacements for Carrick, sources told ESPN.

Carrick's side are without a win in eight games after being beaten by Bournemouth days after the 4-1 Champions League loss at Como.

United have won just two of their 12 matches in all competitions this term and their seven-point return from eight matches represents their worst start to a season since 1986.

The side sit just a point above the Premier League relegation zone in 16th place ahead of Saturday's trip to Chelsea, before heading into the international break with home games against Roma and Aston Villa.

Carrick sidestepped questions over his future following the Bournemouth defeat but appeared to know the writing was on the wall as he waved to the crowd and patted his chest as he exited the pitch, with fans supportively chanting his name.

The Old Trafford faithful's anger was instead aimed at the Glazers, co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Ineos set-up, including United director of football Wilcox.

Players were booed at the final whistle and then fiercely as they followed Carrick down the tunnel on a day when the manager left skipper Bruno Fernandes on the bench.

articles.headline: Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d'Or ahead of Kylian Mbappé, Lamine Yamal; first Englishman in 25 years
articles.description: Harry Kane has become the first Englishman to win the Ballon d'Or in 25 years after beating Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal to the award in London on Saturday.
articles.headlineJa: ハリー・ケインが2026年バロンドールを受賞、キリアン・エムバペとラミン・ヤマルを抑え、イングランド人として25年ぶりの快挙
articles.descriptionJa: 土曜日にロンドンで行われた授賞式で、ハリー・ケインがキリアン・エムバペとラミン・ヤマルを上回り、イングランド人として25年ぶりにバロンドールを受賞した。
articles.body:
Harry Kane has become the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d'Or, beating Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal to claim football's most prestigious individual award.

Kane was presented with the prize -- which is organised by the magazine France Football and voted on by 100 journalists from around the world -- on Monday at a star-studded gala in London, where he was rewarded for a historic season for club and country.

The 33-eyar-old starred for Bayern Munich in the Bundesliga and the Champions League and led England to the World Cup semifinals, scoring 73 goals in the process. He is the fifth English player to ever receive the honour, and the first since Michael Owen in 2005.

"Thank you to everyone who voted for me, I can imagine it was tough, so thank you to everyone who voted for me," an emotional Kane said on stage at the London Palladium Theatre.

Rival Mbappé became the all-time top scorer in World Cup history this summer, with 22 goals, 10 of them scored at this year's edition, while Yamal won the tournament with Spain.

Members of the Ballon d'Or jury choose 10 players, in order, from a 30-player shortlist, with the award going to the player who receives the most points overall.

Kane follows Ousmane Dembélé, who won the prize in 2025, and Rodri who won it in 2024.

For the last two decades, the award was dominated by Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, who top the all-time rankings with eight and five Ballons d'Or respectively.

The Ballon d'Or is seen as the greatest individual prize in football, alongside FIFA's The Best award.

Among the other categories in Monday's ceremony, Yamal was named the Men's Young Player of the Year after starring for Barcelona in LaLiga, and for Spain at the World Cup.

"I'd have liked it to be [teammate Pau] Cubarsi," Yamal said, during a brief speech. "This prize should have been for him. He deserves it."

Spain's Luis de la Fuente won Coach of the Year after guiding Spain to the World Cup, and his first-choice keeper, Unai Simón, was named Men's Goalkeeper of the Year.

articles.headline: Harry Kane thanks Tottenham, pays tribute to England after Ballon d'Or win
articles.description: Harry Kane thanked Tottenham for helping him fulfil his dreams and paid tribute to his international teammates after becoming the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d'Or.
articles.body:
Harry Kane thanked Tottenham for helping him fulfil his dreams and paid tribute to his international teammates after becoming the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d'Or.

The Bayern Munich striker beat Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal to football's most prestigious individual award at a ceremony in London on Monday, becoming the first English winner since Michael Owen in 2001.

Kane, who joined Tottenham at the age of 11 before leaving for Bayern in 2023, reserved a special mention for his former club during his acceptance speech.

"I want to say thank you to Tottenham Hotspur. I wouldn't be where I am today without Tottenham, for sure," Kane said.

"I was there from 11 years old. [With] all the guidance, the coaches, you allowed me to live my dream.

"So, for sure, without all those moments together, all the ups and downs along the way of that journey has led me to this moment here today. So I just want to say thank you to Tottenham Hotspur."

Kane then singled out several coaches who helped him during his time at Spurs, including Chris Ramsey, Tim Sherwood and Ryan Mason, whom he described as one of his best friends.

The 33-year-old, who captained England to third place at the 2026 World Cup, also had praise for his international teammates during a lengthy and emotional speech.

"To all my England teammates. We had a special year," Kane said. "It wasn't the perfect year but we had a lot of good moments.

"We built a great bond together, a lot of togetherness, the way we played and it is truly an honour to play and captain you.

"This one is for all of us, for sure."

He added on coach Thomas Tuchel: "To Thomas Tuchel and the staff, the leadership, the way you drive us, the way you push standards, it is an honour to represent you."

Tuchel, meanwhile, congratulated his captain on becoming just the fifth Englishman to win the Ballon d'Or.

"Congratulations Harry on a deserved Ballon d'Or!" Tuchel said.

"I ran out of superlatives to describe your performances a long time ago, but I'm delighted to see that you have now been formally recognised by the football world.

"To become the first Englishman to win this huge honour in 25 years makes it extra special and we are lucky to have you as our leader.

"I know you will enjoy this moment with your loved ones and then get back to doing what you do best -- scoring goals and winning football matches."

Wembley lit up its gold arches afterwards to mark Kane's historic achievement.

Kane, who also thanked several other coaches and Bayern -- including mentioning manager Vincent Kompany who is currently recovering from a collapse suffered last week -- finished off by saying: "To my wife Kate, my best friend. articles.headline: Cardinals WR Jalen Brooks to miss rest of season with wrist injury
articles.description: Cardinals wide receiver Jalen Brooks posted on social media Monday that he will miss the rest of the season with a wrist injury.
articles.headlineJa: カーディナルスのWRジェイレン・ブルックス、手首の負傷で今季絶望
articles.descriptionJa: カーディナルスのワイドレシーバー、ジェイレン・ブルックスは月曜日、SNSを通じて手首の負傷により今シーズンの残り試合を欠場することを発表した。
articles.body:
TEMPE, Ariz. -- Cardinals wide receiver Jalen Brooks posted on social media Monday that he will miss the rest of the season with a wrist injury that needed "emergency surgery."

Coach Mike LaFleur said Brooks hurt his wrist in the first quarter but didn't mention it to anyone and continued to play.

"That sucks, man," LaFleur said. "What a tough dude.

"Then looking back at it, seeing on the tape, you could see every once in a while, I guess him kind of messing with it a little bit."

Brooks had slid into Marvin Harrison Jr.'s role as the X receiver after Harrison was traded to the Houston Texans on Oct. 11. Brooks had five catches for 81 yards, all of which came after Harrison's trade. He was on pace for a career high in yards.

LaFleur said Brooks' role will be filled by committee.

Rookie Reggie Virgil is expected to get more snaps at the X along with Kendrick Bourne and Simi Fehoko.

The Cardinals could get some help back offensively this week.

Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love is expected to practice Wednesday after missing the last two weeks of practice and the last two games with a left ankle injury. Whether Love plays Sunday is yet to be determined and will be dictated by his week of practice, LaFleur said.

LaFleur feels good about cornerback Max Melton and safety Andrew Wingard, both of whom are dealing with knee injuries, returning to practice Wednesday. Melton missed Sunday's game against the Broncos and Wingard missed the last three.

However, LaFleur does not expect defensive tackle Walter Nolen III to practice Wednesday as he continues to recover from an ankle injury that kept him out Sunday.

articles.headline: Giants' Cam Skattebo, John Harbaugh object to lowering helmet penalty
articles.description: Giants coach John Harbaugh and Cam Skattebo took issue with a first-quarter penalty call Sunday against Houston, when the running back was flagged for unnecessary roughness for impermissible helmet contact.
articles.headlineJa: ジャイアンツのカム・スカッテボとジョン・ハーボーがヘルメット下げの反則判定に異議
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜日のヒューストン戦の第1クォーターで、ランニングバックのスカッテボが不適切なヘルメット接触による「不必要なラフネス」の反則を科されたことに対し、ジョン・ハーボーコーチとスカッテボが不満を表明した。
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- The New York Giants might have won and played their most complete game Sunday against the Houston Texans, but running back Cam Skattebo and coach John Harbaugh aren't happy with the way one play was officiated.

Harbaugh and Skattebo disagreed with a penalty call in the first quarter when Skattebo was flagged for a personal foul -- unnecessary roughness -- for impermissible helmet contact.

Skattebo was penalized for lowering his head into a defender on the first-quarter run that originally went for a 7-yard gain. It sent Houston safety M.J. Stewart flying to the ground when the two collided and left Skattebo and Harbaugh visibly upset with the call. 

Skattebo still wasn't happy after the Giants' 27-21 overtime victory, in which he had his first 100-yard rushing game. He finished with a career-high 124 yards on 17 carries.

"The NFL loves to post me [on social media] when I do stuff like that, but also wants to take stuff from me," Skattebo said Sunday. "I'm going to run the ball like I want to run the ball. And if I'm going to continue to get flagged for it or fined for it, I guess I'm going to play for free. I'm going to do what I can to be on this team and give everything I got. If they're going to punish me for that, then I'm just going to keep doing it and playing hard."

This wasn't the first time Skattebo has been called out for the infraction. He was fined $7,073 earlier this month for "illegal helmet contact on a running play."

Harbaugh was shown on the game's television broadcast vehemently objecting to the call, and was in the linesman's ear for a while after the play.

"That's how I felt about it," Harbaugh said Monday. "You can't run in there and give tacklers your chest. When you run low, your head's down there, too. You can't move your head off your shoulders. It's a physical impossibility."

The NFL has made it a point to deemphasize offensive players using their helmets as weapons. It's still rare that the infraction involves a penalty flag.

It caught Harbaugh by surprise.

"It did," he said. "It certainly did, yes."

Skattebo, the second-year running back out of Arizona State, is known for his physical style of play. He often seeks out the contact.

But Harbaugh didn't seem to think there was any kind of intent to do so with his helmet.

"I'm quite sure [Skattebo is] not trying to use his helmet as a weapon, as a battering ram. It's not the way he's thinking," Harbaugh said. "He's leading with his shoulder. That's what he's trying to do. ... So, I didn't have a problem with the technique personally at all, but we haven't heard from the league. Maybe they'll be able to enlighten us a little bit on it in terms of what they want us to teach, and that would be great."

The controversy comes one week after Skattebo saw his role greatly reduced in a loss to the New Orleans Saints. He viewed it as punishment for several costly fumbles, including late in a tie against the Washington Commanders.

articles.headline: Steelers Aaron Rodgers, QB room lead NFL Week 7's best arrivals
articles.description: NFL stars continue to turn game-day arrivals into their own weekly fashion showcase.
articles.headlineJa: スティーラーズのアロン・ロジャースらQB陣がNFL第7週の「ベスト・アライバル」を牽引
articles.descriptionJa: NFLのスター選手たちは、試合会場への到着時の装いを、毎週のファッションショーのように楽しみ続けている。
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback room set the fashion standard high Sunday in Paris, simulating European-style looks from their favorite show "Peaky Blinders" with three-piece suits and flat caps.

The idea spawned from backup quarterback Mason Rudolph, who reached out to clothing designer Mitch Purgason to have the suits custom-made for this game.

Rudolph explained that the Steelers quarterback room bonds over "Peaky Blinders." The show is extremely British, not French. But Rudolph's idea was to lean into United Kingdom experience and display with energy that they connect with personally.

Purgason said he flew up to Pittsburgh to custom-fit the Steelers quarterback room 13 days ago, then he and his associate stylist, Rachel Leskowsky, went to work making the suits in about nine days. Purgason then flew up to hand-deliver the fits last minute before their flight to Paris.

The work is worth it for looks as clean as the Steelers quarterback room. They posed for pregame pictures in Paris, and it exuded boss energy. Will this lead to more NFL positional groups leaning into translating their personal connection niche into fashion?

Here are Week 7's most fashionable NFL player gameday fits that caught our eye:

Monday night drip

Ahead of "Monday Night Football" against the Philadelphia Eagles, Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott rocked a mint green suede bomber jack for a clean look. The starting quarterback on the other side, Tanner McKee, wore a suit that included a special message -- images of his family are sewn inside his jacket.

Sunday's best

A return game for Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III on "Sunday Night Football" prompted a simple, yet sleek outfit. He wore all-white ahead of his first game against the Seattle Seahawks since signing with Kansas City in the offseason. His fellow teammates, Patrick Mahomes, Travis Kelce, Chris Jones and L'Jarius Sneed, all rocked suits.

It was tracksuits galore in the afternoon slate, with Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald styling a black look with a pair of shades. Meanwhile, Raiders defensive end Maxx Crosby broke out a white jumpsuit, showing off his ink with an unzipped jacket.

Though Sunday marked a holiday in National Tight Ends Day, that didn't stop Rodgers and the Steelers quarterback room from channeling their inner "Peaky Blinders" in Paris with coordinated suits, boots, flat cap and all.

Thursday's looks

Caleb Williams kept it sharp ahead of "Thursday Night Football," pairing a navy suit with a black crewneck shirt. The Chicago Bears quarterback skipped the tie but not the wired earbuds. Naturally, he had his matcha drink in one hand and a structured brown leather bag in the other.

articles.headline: Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace injured: What's next for the OKC Thunder?
articles.description: The Thunder will be without two starting guards for months. Could they make a trade to try to replace Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace?
articles.headlineJa: ジェイレン・ウィリアムズとケイソン・ウォレスが負傷：OKCサンダーの次なる一手は？
articles.descriptionJa: サンダーは数ヶ月にわたり、先発ガード2名が欠場することになる。ジェイレン・ウィリアムズとケイソン・ウォレスの穴を埋めるため、トレードに踏み切るのだろうか？
articles.body:
The Oklahoma City Thunder lost two starters to long-term injuries in their 108-101 win over the LA Clippers on Sunday night.

General manager Sam Presti announced Monday that guard Jalen Williams will undergo surgery for a dislocated left ankle and fractured fibula, while guard Cason Wallace will undergo surgery for a torn labrum in his left shoulder. Both players are expected to miss several months.

Williams was placed on a stretcher and wheeled off the court after he was injured on a drive to the basket late in the fourth quarter. Wallace left the game in the first quarter and didn't return.

They're both big losses for the Thunder, who were counting on Williams to get back to his All-Star form from the 2024-25 season and Wallace to step into the starting lineup. Williams missed 49 regular-season games last season while recovering from surgery on his right wrist and then injuring both hamstrings. He played in just five games -- and 107 total minutes -- in the postseason as OKC was beaten by the San Antonio Spurs in seven games in the Western Conference finals. Wallace signed a five-year, $139 million contract extension just before the season began.

How bad do these injuries hurt the Thunder, who are 3-0 and believe they have the talent to make it back to the NBA Finals? Do they have flexibility to make a move to replace Williams or Wallace? ESPN's reporters and analysts weigh in:

What was the early word on Williams' injury inside the Thunder?

Emotional devastation, as evidenced by Shai Gilgeous-Alexander tearing up on the court.

It's gut-wrenching any time a player suffers a gruesome injury, but hearts are especially heavy for Williams in Oklahoma City. This is a young star who has had horrific injury luck despite doing everything right in terms of conditioning and rehab. 

Williams' performance during the 2025 title run -- toughing it out with a shooting wrist that required surgery and still delivering 40 points in pivotal Game 5 of the NBA Finals -- will always be legendary in Oklahoma City. His injury misfortune has been miserable since with recurring hamstring strains that robbed him of most of last season and this cruel twist a week into this season.

The Thunder are a tight-knit team that has had to deal with the emotional consequences that come with the business of basketball. It stung to see title-winning teammates Luguentz Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins traded in salary-slashing deals. This injury causes a deeper pain that the Thunder will have to process while figuring out how to fill a massive hole in the lineup. -- Tim MacMahon

How big of a hole will these losses leave for Oklahoma City?

These two injuries are the most important development of the new season's first week in terms of how they change the championship picture. The Thunder still have excellent depth and star power at the guard and center positions, but they already shed a fair amount of perimeter depth over the summer by trading Dort, Wiggins and Joe.
